title: Unresolved identity report
description: One row of data/curated/identity-unresolved.jsonl: a source string that named no entity the source registers. This is the report that makes resolution visible rather than silent — the same job event-selection.jsonl does for the event rule. `no-source-identity` means the string became a new entity with its ID anchored on the string itself, so a later registry row with that exact name keeps the same ID; `ambiguous` means the string names more than one entity and nothing is minted, because picking one would merge two distinct people. An empty file means every reference in this corpus resolved.

name.description: The minted entity's display name — the string itself — so the report reads without decoding an ID (spec R12). For an ambiguous string, the string itself.

id.description: The entity minted for this string, or null for an ambiguity, where minting would hide the problem.

firstSeen.description: Earliest UTC date on which a recorded source row used this string.

lastSeen.description: Latest UTC date on which a recorded source row used this string.

reason.description: Why this string is here: nothing in the source registers it, or several entities answer to it.

candidates.description: For `ambiguous`, the canonical IDs the string could mean. Empty for `no-source-identity`.
